title: account-api Latency and Cache Diagnostics
text:
### Scope
This runbook applies to latency degradation affecting account-api. Diagnostic signals must not be presented as confirmed root cause unless the incident record explicitly confirms them.

### Cache diagnostics
When p95 latency is elevated, compare it with the service baseline. If cache hit ratio falls below 80%, inspect cache eviction rate, key churn, backend fetch latency and recent cache policy changes. Compare each value with the pre-incident baseline.

A reduced cache hit ratio is a diagnostic signal. It does not by itself prove that cache behavior is the root cause.

### Safe actions
Reading telemetry, checking dashboards and comparing baselines are safe diagnostic actions. Do not flush, restart or reconfigure the cache without explicit approval from the Incident Commander.

title: Production Change Readiness Policy
text:
### Rollback readiness
For account-api production changes, a rollback plan must exist and the latest successful rollback rehearsal must have completed within the previous 30 days. A rehearsal older than 30 days does not satisfy the production readiness gate.

The rehearsal must have succeeded. A scheduled rehearsal or a documented plan without execution does not count as evidence.

### Security-sensitive changes
Changes affecting authentication, authorization, secrets or token lifecycle also require an approved security review with no open blockers.

### Evidence
Statements such as "tests executed", "rollback documented" or "security review requested" do not count as PASS unless the required result is available.

title: Legacy Deployment Handbook
text:
### Historical rollback rule
This handbook previously allowed account-api production changes when a successful rollback rehearsal had been completed within the previous 90 days.

### Current use
The 90-day requirement was used before the 2026 Production Change Readiness Policy was introduced. This document is retained for historical reference only and must not override active production policy.

title: Customer Incident Communication Policy
text:
### Outage terminology
For account-api, if service availability remains above 99.8% and application error rate remains below 1%, Support should describe the event as a degradation, not a complete outage. An Incident Commander may explicitly override this classification when customer impact is not captured by those metrics.

### Regional impact
For incidents limited to one region, Support must identify the affected region and must not imply that unaffected regions have the same impact.

### Root cause
Support may communicate a root cause as confirmed only when the incident record explicitly contains rca_status = confirmed. An engineering hypothesis is not a confirmed root cause.

title: Historical Incident INC-6310
text:
### Symptoms
INC-6310 affected account-api. Symptoms included elevated latency, timeouts and degraded account operations.

### Confirmed cause
The confirmed root cause for INC-6310 was database connection-pool exhaustion following a deployment that increased query concurrency. This root cause applies only to INC-6310 and must not be used as evidence of the root cause of another incident merely because symptoms are similar.

### Remediation
The team rolled back the query-concurrency change and added improved database pool saturation monitoring. The postmortem does not specify the maximum configured connection-pool size.

title: account-api Capacity Planning Notes
text:
### Capacity planning
Capacity planning for account-api tracks CPU headroom, memory, request rate, database utilization and cache efficiency. The document contains quarterly growth projections and load-test targets.

### Database
Database connection-pool utilization is an important saturation signal. This document intentionally does not define the production maximum connection-pool size because that value is managed by runtime configuration and may differ by environment.

title: account-api Runtime Architecture
text:
### Request path
account-api uses a distributed cache for session-adjacent metadata and a relational database for durable account records. Cache misses can increase backend fetch work but are not themselves proof of a database or cache fault.

### Observability
Latency investigations should correlate p50, p95, cache hit ratio, backend fetch latency and database saturation. Architecture documentation describes dependencies; it does not define incident severity or rollback readiness policy.

title: account-api Observability Signals
text:
### Latency alerts
The warning alert fires when p95 latency exceeds 650 ms for ten minutes. The critical alert fires at 1000 ms for five minutes. Alert thresholds are detection aids, not automatic root-cause statements.

### Cache signals
Cache hit ratio below 80% raises a diagnostic advisory. Operators should correlate eviction rate and backend fetch latency before drawing conclusions.

title: Customer Account FAQ
text:
### General information
The account service provides profile management, session management and access to customer settings. Customers experiencing difficulties are advised to retry after a short period and contact Support if the problem continues.

### Operational scope
This public FAQ does not expose internal incident thresholds, rollback requirements, infrastructure configuration or diagnostic runbooks.

title: Operations Retrospective Notes
text:
### Team observations
The team discussed alert quality, documentation cleanup and on-call handover. An informal comment states that many account-api latency incidents eventually involve cache or database behavior.

### Evidence warning
This is a generalization and is not valid evidence of the root cause of a specific incident. The team recommended making active policies easier to distinguish from legacy documents.

title: account-api Disaster Recovery Standard
text:
### Recovery objectives
account-api has an RTO of 30 minutes and an RPO of 5 minutes for regional disaster recovery scenarios.

### Scope
These objectives apply to regional recovery. They do not replace the production change rollback rehearsal requirement and do not define how recently a rollback rehearsal must have run.

title: account-api Service Level Objectives
text:
### Availability objective
The monthly availability objective is 99.95%.

### Latency objective
The p95 objective for normal traffic is 500 ms. SLO breaches trigger investigation but do not automatically classify a complete outage or authorize a restart.

title: General Incident Severity Matrix
text:
### Purpose
This matrix defines broad organizational severity language. Service-specific policies may impose more precise thresholds.

### Rule
Operators should prefer service-specific active policy when it exists. Historical incident labels are not a substitute for current classification criteria.

title: Observability Platform User Guide
text:
### Dashboards
The observability platform exposes latency, errors, availability and saturation across services.

### Interpretation
Metrics are evidence inputs. The platform does not determine root cause or authorize remediation actions.

title: Change Management Glossary
text:
### Terms
A rollback plan describes how to revert a change. A rollback rehearsal is evidence that the procedure was executed successfully. Approval is a separate governance decision.

### Scope
The glossary defines terms but not service-specific time windows.

title: Knowledge Base Authoring Standard
text:
### Metadata
Operational documents should include owner, status, date and service scope. Superseded content must remain identifiable.

### Retrieval
Search relevance does not imply authority. Consumers must consider document status and scope.

title: SRE On-call Handover Guide
text:
### Handover
Record active incidents, working hypotheses, pending approvals and next diagnostic steps. Label hypotheses clearly.

### Restrictions
A handover note is not an authoritative production policy.

title: Shared Platform Note 01
text:

When a service-specific ACTIVE policy or runbook exists, that material takes precedence over generic shared guidance for thresholds, rollback readiness and diagnostic procedures.

### Retrieval note
Shared documents may rank for broad terms such as latency, rollback, incident or monitoring. Relevance alone does not make them the authoritative answer for a specific service.
